name: Minimal Gallery
tagline: 2,961 hand-picked minimal websites, tagged by industry, with an open WordPress REST API
description: A curated showcase of minimal website design that Piet Terheyden has run daily since 2013. It holds 2,961 website entries, 181 third-party website templates and 102 tools, cross-tagged with 68 industry and page-type tags such as Portfolio (971), Agency (750), E-commerce (139), One page (122) and Pricing (96). The whole index is server-rendered HTML and is also readable as JSON through the site's exposed WordPress REST API, so an agent can list every entry and its outbound URL without scraping thumbnails. It is aimed at designers and developers looking for reference marketing sites and portfolios.

pricing_detail: Free to browse. No paywall, no login. Revenue comes from sponsor slots and a submission flow.
agent_guidance: This is the rare inspiration gallery an agent can actually read: hit https://minimal.gallery/wp-json/wp/v2/posts (plus the custom `template` and `tool` types) and you get JSON titles and links, with X-WP-Total giving exact counts. Reach for it when you need real-world reference URLs for a marketing site, portfolio or pricing page and then fetch the target sites themselves — Minimal Gallery gives you the pointer, not the markup. Do not expect code, tokens or components here; pair it with a component library from the index for the actual build.
why_it_matters: One of the longest-running curated web galleries still updated by hand, and its accidental REST API makes it one of the few design galleries a machine can enumerate rather than merely look at.

name: Dark Mode Design
tagline: About 369 hand-picked dark-UI websites, one curator, no tags and no filters
description: A single-topic gallery of websites built dark-first, curated by Cai Cardenas. Pagination runs to 24 pages of 16 thumbnails, so the collection is roughly 369 entries; each card is a screenshot plus an outbound link to the live site. There is no taxonomy, no search and no filtering — you page through it. Submission is by email, there is no login wall, and the pages are server-rendered Webflow HTML that a fetcher can read.
pricing_detail: Free. Submissions are free by email to hello@darkmodedesign.com. A sponsored Mobbin placement appears on the grid.
agent_guidance: Use it only when the brief is specifically a dark-first interface and you want live reference sites to fetch and study; the whole index is walkable via the Webflow query param `?60a99e98_page=N` for N in 1..24, and each page yields 16 outbound URLs from plain HTML. Because there are no tags, you cannot filter by industry or page type — go to Minimal Gallery for that and come here only for the dark-palette question. It gives you zero code, tokens or contrast values, so pair it with a real contrast checker before you copy any palette you see.
why_it_matters: Dark mode is where most design systems quietly fall apart, and a focused corpus of sites that got it right is more useful than a general gallery filtered to 'dark'.
notable_for: outbound links readable from static HTML
evidence: https://darkmodedesign.com (301 to https://www.darkmodedesign.com/), https://www.darkmodedesign.com/about, pagination probes https://www.darkmodedesign.com/?60a99e98_page=1,10,20,21,22,23,24 (16 outbound links per page through page 23, 1 on page 24)

name: Unsplash
tagline: 8.7M free-to-use photos with a free JSON API at 1,000 requests/hour
description: Unsplash is a library of 8.7 million photographs from 428.4k photographers, released under the bespoke Unsplash License: free for commercial and non-commercial use, no permission and no attribution legally required. Its developer API is free, covers search, single-photo and listing endpoints, returns full metadata (dimensions, dominant colour, EXIF, raw/full/regular/small/thumb URLs) and allows 1,000 requests per hour on the free tier. Official client libraries exist for JavaScript, PHP, Ruby, iOS and Android. It is the default source when a build needs real photographic imagery rather than placeholders.
pricing_detail: Browsing and downloading are free. API free tier: 1,000 requests/hour, all endpoints. An Enterprise plan (price not published) raises limits and unlocks Unsplash+ images. Unsplash+ is a paid subscriber tier for members.
agent_guidance: Reach for Unsplash when a page needs credible photographic imagery and you want it fetched programmatically — `npm install unsplash-js`, an access key, and you can search and drop in `photo.urls.regular` with on-the-fly resize and crop params baked into the URL. Three API rules bite in production and none of them are optional: you must hotlink the `photo.urls` values rather than rehost, you must attribute the photographer with a `?utm_source=<app>&utm_medium=referral` link, and you must ping `photo.links.download_location` on any download-like action or your production approval gets rejected. Do not build a wallpaper app or an unofficial Unsplash client on it — both are explicitly banned, and unmodified photos may not be resold.
why_it_matters: It is the only stock photo library at this scale with a genuinely free, well-documented, machine-readable API, which makes it the one an agent can actually wire into a build.
notable_for: no attribution legally required for the images
official JS, PHP, Ruby, iOS and Android SDKs
on-the-fly image resize params in every URL
evidence: https://unsplash.com, https://unsplash.com/license, https://unsplash.com/developers, https://help.unsplash.com/en/articles/2511245-unsplash-api-guidelines, https://registry.npmjs.org/unsplash-js (unsplash-js 8.0.1, MIT, published 2026-08-14)

name: Pexels
tagline: Free stock photos and video, free API at 200 req/hour and 20,000/month
description: Pexels is a free stock library covering both photography and video, under the Pexels License: free for commercial and non-commercial use, modification allowed, attribution appreciated but not required for the media itself. Its API is free with a key from any Pexels account and covers photo search, curated photos, video search, popular videos and collections, rate-limited to 200 requests per hour and 20,000 per month. Unlike Unsplash it carries a real stock video catalogue, which makes it the go-to when a hero section needs footage rather than a still. Total library size is not published.
pricing_detail: Free, including the API. No paid tier for access; higher rate limits are granted free on request when you attribute properly.
agent_guidance: Pick Pexels over Unsplash when the brief needs video — it is the free library with a real stock footage catalogue and a `/v1/videos/search` endpoint — and treat photos as a second opinion when an Unsplash search comes back thin. Two traps: the API asks you to credit the photographer as 'Photo by X on Pexels' with a link back even though the media licence itself does not require it, and the 200 req/hour ceiling is five times tighter than Unsplash's, so cache aggressively rather than querying per render. The public site 403s a plain curl with a default user agent, so scrape through the API with a key, not the HTML.
why_it_matters: The free-video half of the stock problem has almost no credible free-API answer, and Pexels is it.
notable_for: free stock video with a search API
attribution optional on the licence, requested by the API
evidence: https://www.pexels.com (WebFetch 200; plain curl returns 403), https://www.pexels.com/license/, https://www.pexels.com/api/, https://www.pexels.com/api/documentation/, https://registry.npmjs.org/pexels (pexels 1.4.0, MIT, published 2022-09-19)

name: unDraw
tagline: ~1,760 recolourable SVG illustrations, free commercially, no attribution
description: unDraw is an open-content illustration library by Katerina Limpitsouni, with roughly 1,760 flat-vector scenes (44 pages of 40 in the browser). Every illustration recolours to a single accent hex on the fly before download, which is why unDraw art blends into a product's brand instead of fighting it. The licence permits commercial and non-commercial use with no permission and no credit, but forbids redistribution as packs, building a competing library, automated scraping, and using the assets to train or fine-tune AI models. It is the default illustration set for empty states, 404 pages and onboarding in web products.
pricing_detail: Free, no account. unDraw+ is an optional supporter tier that adds features such as animated scenes; price not published on the public pages.
agent_guidance: This is the illustration set to reach for whenever a screen needs a friendly graphic and the brand has one accent colour — no attribution string to thread through the footer, and inline SVG means it recolours with `currentColor` or a CSS variable once you drop it in. There is an undocumented public endpoint, `https://undraw.co/api/search?q=<term>`, returning 40 results per page as JSON with a direct `https://cdn.undraw.co/illustration/<slug>.svg` URL — useful for finding the right slug, but the licence explicitly forbids automated bulk downloading and forbids using the assets to train or fine-tune AI models, so use it to look up one asset, never to mirror the library. Prefer it over Storyset when you do not want an attribution obligation; prefer Storyset when you need animation.
why_it_matters: The recolour-to-your-brand step is what separates unDraw from every other free illustration pack — it is the only one that reliably stops looking like a stock illustration.
notable_for: licence bans AI training and scraping
evidence: https://undraw.co/illustrations (200; __NEXT_DATA__ shows 40 illustrations per page, "totalPages":44), https://undraw.co/license, https://undraw.co/api/search?q=chat (200, JSON: results/total/hasMore/page, 40 per page, cdn.undraw.co SVG URLs)

name: Storyset
tagline: Freepik's editable illustrations in 5 styles, animatable, attribution required
description: Storyset is Freepik Company's illustration platform: every concept is drawn in five named styles — Rafiki, Bro, Amico, Pana and Cuate — across six categories (business, education, medical, technology, people, multi-purpose). An in-browser editor lets you change the accent colour, toggle the background between Hidden, Simple and Detailed, edit layers, and animate the scene before exporting SVG or PNG; a Figma plugin mirrors the same catalogue. Free use requires crediting Storyset; the terms route unattributed and commercial-heavy use to a paid Freepik/Flaticon Premium subscription. It suits teams that want illustrations with motion and a consistent house style across a whole product.
pricing_detail: Free with attribution to Storyset. Removing the attribution requirement and the broader commercial grant run through a paid Freepik/Flaticon Premium subscription; the price is not stated on Storyset's own pages.
agent_guidance: Choose Storyset over unDraw only when you specifically need motion — the animate step and the five consistent styles are the reason it exists — and accept that you owe a visible credit line, which is a real product decision, not a formality. There is no API, no npm package and no bulk export: the pipeline is a human in the browser editor exporting SVG or PNG, or the Figma plugin, so do not plan an automated asset step around it. The terms are also genuinely ambiguous about where free-with-credit ends and Freepik Premium begins, so flag the licence question to the user before shipping Storyset art in a commercial product.
why_it_matters: It is the most complete free illustration system with animation and a coherent multi-style house look, and the attribution string is the price of that.
notable_for: attribution required unless you pay Freepik
evidence: https://storyset.com, https://storyset.com/terms, https://storyset.com/illustration/chatting/rafiki, https://storyset.com/business, https://storyset.com/search?q=chat. No total illustration count is published anywhere on the site; https://storyset.com/illustrations returns 404 and there is no sitemap.xml.
